correctly. I removed all other logic just to verify this very simple thing is working. /setup.ts process.env.LOG_LEVEL = 'trace'; process.env.LOG_LEVEL_CONSOLE = 'silent'; process.env.PORT = '8081'; process.env.PROTOCOL = "http"; import { ConfigureHooks } from "@common"; if (ConfigureHooks.name == "") { console.log("Yea"); } When I try to run tests, I use npm run test which run the npm script: TS_NODE_PROJECT='./test/tsconfig.json' mocha --require ts-node/register --require tsconfig-paths/register test/**/mytest.spec.ts --exit The path is set to only run mytest.spec.ts right now, but once this is resolved I'll switch it back to **/* . As for ConfigureHooks , it is most certainly a function. It is defined as export const ConfigureHooks = <T extends IMetadata>(MetaSchema<T>): void => {... unrelated logic... }; Finally, it's important to note that I can build and execute the project (I can run the server) and manually test the actions I'm trying to automate tests for myself. So I know I don't have something wrong, causing build failure, in my tsconfig or any of my import references/paths/etc. What is appears to me is that Mocha is just not using the tsconfig.json and therefore it's not pathing correctly. Here the contents of my tsconfig files. (I am aware CommonJS is depreciated. Once I get things back to 'working' I will start upgrading and future-proofing.
